title: Nrf2/STAT3-mediated activation of SLC6A3 underlies the neuroprotective effect of quercetin in ischemic stroke.
authors: Cai, Huabao; Zhao, Meng-Yu; Wang, Cun-Zhi; Wang, Jin-Ni; Tang, Wen-Ping; Mao, Wen-Bao; Feng, Shi; Ding, Fang-Fang; Ke, Jing; Shi, Ting-Ting; Wang, Yuan; Yu, Tian-Hang; Xu, Wan-Yan; Wang, Li-Na; Chen, Juan; Gong, Ying-Jie; Zhang, Song; Xu, Jia-Feng; Chen, Guan-Jun; Qian, Yu; Ding, Yan-Yu
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究槲皮素通过Nrf2/STAT3调控SLC6A3在缺血性卒中中的神经保护作用，虽涉及转录因子与DNA结合，但核心是疾病机制与湿实验验证，无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题TF-DNA互作建模无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability, yet effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Oxidative stress and dopaminergic dysfunction are key contributors to neuronal injury following cerebral ischemia. Quercetin, a natural flavonoid with antioxidant properties, has shown promise in preclinical models; however, its precise mechanisms of action remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We employed a combination of network pharmacology, in vivo middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) models, and in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) assays. Bioinformatics analyses identified potential therapeutic targets of quercetin, which were validated through Western blotting, immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, CRISPR-Cas9, and co-immunoprecipitation. Functional outcomes were evaluated via behavioral tests, TUNEL staining, and oxidative stress marker assays. RESULTS: Quercetin significantly reduced cerebral edema, improved neurological function, and inhibited neuronal apoptosis following MCAO. Mechanistically, quercetin activated the Nrf2/STAT3 signaling pathway, promoting nuclear translocation of Nrf2 and transcriptional upregulation of the dopamine transporter gene SLC6A3. This regulatory axis was critical for mitigating oxidative DNA damage and preserving neuronal integrity. Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified Nrf2, STAT3, and SLC6A3 as core targets of quercetin. Inhibition of Nrf2 or STAT3 abrogated the protective effects of quercetin in both in vitro and in vivo models. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings identify the Nrf2/STAT3/SLC6A3 axis as a key mediator of quercetin's neuroprotective effects in ischemic stroke. To our knowledge, this is the first study to identify the Nrf2/STAT3/SLC6A3 axis as a key regulatory pathway underlying the neuroprotective action of quercetin.
abstract_zh: 背景：缺血性卒中（Ischemic stroke, IS）是死亡和长期残疾的主要原因，但有效的神经保护策略仍然有限。氧化应激和多巴胺能功能障碍是脑缺血后神经元损伤的关键因素。槲皮素（Quercetin）是一种具有抗氧化特性的天然黄酮类化合物，在临床前模型中显示出潜力；然而，其确切作用机制仍未完全阐明。方法：我们结合了网络药理学、体内大脑中动脉闭塞（middle cerebral artery occlusion, MCAO）模型和体外氧糖剥夺/再灌注（oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion, OGD/R）实验。生物信息学分析确定了槲皮素的潜在治疗靶点，并通过Western blotting、免疫荧光、qRT-PCR、CRISPR-Cas9和免疫共沉淀进行了验证。功能结果通过行为测试、TUNEL染色和氧化应激标志物检测进行评估。结果：槲皮素显著减轻了MCAO后的脑水肿，改善了神经功能，并抑制了神经元凋亡。机制上，槲皮素激活了Nrf2/STAT3信号通路，促进Nrf2核转位和多巴胺转运蛋白基因SLC6A3的转录上调。这一调控轴对于减轻氧化性DNA损伤和维持神经元完整性至关重要。网络药理学和分子对接确定了Nrf2、STAT3和SLC6A3为槲皮素的核心靶点。抑制Nrf2或STAT3在体外和体内模型中均消除了槲皮素的保护作用。结论：我们的发现确定了Nrf2/STAT3/SLC6A3轴是槲皮素在缺血性卒中中神经保护作用的关键介导因子。据我们所知，这是首次将Nrf2/STAT3/SLC6A3轴确定为槲皮素神经保护作用的关键调控通路的研究。
